column1: # The Synology package table: the DSM generations HyperDrop builds for, the
# package families, and every Synology PLATFORM that maps onto a family. The
# one source for build-spk.sh (what each .spk is built for), build-feed.sh
# (which feeds exist), the maps in hyperdrop-site.nginx.conf (what Package
# Center is answered) and the build list on website/downloads/synology/index.html
# (which build the page selects). arches.py reads it and rewrites the
# generated blocks; site:check runs it and diffs.
# Tab-separated. Blank lines and lines starting with # are ignored.
#   A DSM generation a package is built for. DSM refuses a package whose
#   os_min_ver major differs from its own (install error 261), so every
#   generation gets its own .spk per family, stamped with this os_min_ver.
#   name is the package's label (hyperdrop-<version>-dsm<major>-<name>.spk and
#   feed/dsm<major>-<name>.json). majors is a comma-separated list of the dsm
#   generations the family is built for. The DSM 7 INFO arch is the INFO
#   file's arch value there: a space-separated list of Synology package
#   arches, * for every platform row of the family, or - for a family DSM 7
#   never gets. Synology calls the 64-bit ARM package family armv8; several
#   older 32-bit ARM platforms have their own package arch rather than
#   belonging to the armv7 family, but run the same GOARM=7 binary. DSM 6
#   matches INFO arch against the box's platform name, so its packages always
#   list every platform row of the family. label is what the download page
#   Package Center asks by PLATFORM, not by CPU: a DS1522+ asks with
#   arch=r1000, never arch=x86_64 (measured against DSM 7.4.1-90080). Names
#   from SynoCommunity's toolchain set. x86 and evansport only ever ran DSM 6;
#   a DSM 7 box never asks with them. 88f6281 (ARMv5, kernel 2.6.32, older
#   than any Go runtime supports) and ppc853x/qoriq (PowerPC, which Go cannot
#   build for in 32 bits) are deliberately absent, since no package is built
